background.fact: RA belongs to the RealNetworks RealAudio family of compressed sound formats.
RealAudio was used for online sound delivery from the mid-1990s onward.
The RealAudio 10 family includes AAC, RealAudio, lossless and multichannel coding options.
The .ra ending can identify audio delivered through the RealMedia system.
The Library of Congress lists audio/vnd.rn-realaudio as a vendor-associated media type for RA.
RealAudio is proprietary, with limited publicly available technical documentation.
RealAudio files can contain descriptive information such as a title or artist.

windows.note: Reads RealMedia media through its demuxers; this is a command-line converter, not a graphical player.
Portable player using FFmpeg libraries; format and codec support depend on its build.
The free PC player explicitly lists RA and RealAudio Lossless among supported audio types.

problems.fact: A .ram companion is a streaming metafile; it is not interchangeable with the sound file itself.
An RA extension alone does not identify its audio codec; the family includes several different coding systems.
Playback requires a decoder for the particular RealAudio variant; FFmpeg lists separate decoders for multiple RealAudio codecs.

background.fact: WTV is Microsoft Windows Media Center recording storage, written through the Stream Buffer Engine.
Microsoft documented WTV for developers in September 2008.
WTV superseded DVR-MS and uses a different underlying file structure rather than ASF.
A recording can combine MPEG-2 pictures with MPEG-1 Layer II or AC-3 audio.
The format carries descriptive metadata and rights-management information alongside the media.
The Stream Buffer Engine normally saves television recordings beneath the public Recorded TV directory.
WTV can signal changes in video resolution or compression while a recording is being read.

windows.note: Reads WTV media through its demuxers; this is a command-line converter, not a graphical player.
Portable player using FFmpeg libraries; format and codec support depend on its build.
Historical Microsoft playback environment; protected broadcasts may require the PC that recorded them.

mac.note: Reads WTV media through its demuxers; this is a command-line converter, not a graphical player.
Portable player using FFmpeg libraries; format and codec support depend on its build.

linux.note: Reads WTV media through its demuxers; this is a command-line converter, not a graphical player.
Portable player using FFmpeg libraries; format and codec support depend on its build.

problems.fact: A broadcaster can restrict a protected recording to playback on its original Media Center computer.
A DVR-MS-only application needs a compatible copy; Windows 7 supplied WTVConverter.exe for this conversion.
Software reading WTV must handle media-type changes rather than assuming fixed video and audio properties throughout.
